newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Little Swan says it hits 96 profit goal.
newsitem.headline: Little Swan says it hits 96 profit goal.

text.p: Jiangsu-based washing machine producer Wuxi Little Swan Co Ltd beat its 1996 net profit target of 175 million yuan, up from 147 million yuan for 1995, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
The higher earnings were based on sales which topped one million units in 1996 against 800,000 in 1995, the spokesman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Precise results would not be made public until after an audit was completed, he added.

The official said Little Swan was likely to post stronger earnings for 1997 due in part to the expected contribution from a joint venture with German company Bosch-Siemens Household Appliances Co Ltd.
Little Swan owns 40 percent and Bosch-Siemens the remaining 60 percent in the US$25 million BSW Household Appliances Ltd in the city of Wuxi in eastern Jiangsu province, the official said.
The venture, opened last October, was designed to turn out 400,000 washing machines a year, he said.
BSW's products, carrying the brandname "Siemens," are largely sold in mainland China, the official said. He gave no profit forecast for the venture.

The official said Little Swan planned to issue 50 million A shares in the first half of this year and use the proceeds to expand washing machine output to 1.5 million units annually by 2000. He gave no further details.

In its 1996 interim report, Little Swan said it had audited net earnings of 96.82 million yuan in the first half of 1996, up 20.72 percent from 80.20 million yuan in the year-earlier period, using Chinese accounting standards.
